title: Per-Attack Blocking Hides Catalog Vulnerability: A Weakest-Link Analysis of Tool Manifests
abstract: arXiv:2611.31338v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Runtime controls for tool-using agents depend on manifests that state what each tool may read and where its output may go. Evaluations of these controls, including ChainCaps, report per-attack blocking: the share of attacks a set of manifests stops. We show that this is the wrong unit. A catalog is only as safe as its weakest source policy: if $M$ independently authored policies are each wrong with probability $p$, the chance that the catalog contains an accepted exfiltration path is $1-(1-p)^M$, while per-attack blocking stays at $1-p$. Three lines of evidence agree. In synthetic catalogs run through two enforcement engines, ChainCaps and OpenAPPA, per-attack blocking holds at 92% while catalog vulnerability rises from 22% at 10 tools to 99% at 200, and composition provides no protective effect. translated_title: 单攻击拦截率掩盖了工具目录漏洞：工具清单的最弱环节分析
translated_abstract: 面向使用工具的智能体的运行时安全控制依赖于清单，这些清单声明了每个工具可以读取什么内容以及其输出可以流向何处。对此类控制（包括 ChainCaps）的评估通常报告“单攻击拦截率”，即一组清单能够阻止的攻击比例。我们证明这是一个错误的评估单位。一个工具目录的安全性取决于其最弱的来源策略：如果 M 个独立编写的策略各自以概率 p 出错，那么目录中存在一条被放行的数据外泄路径的概率为 1-(1-p)^M，而单攻击拦截率却始终停留在 1-p。三方面证据相互印证：在通过两个执行引擎运行的合成目录实验中，单攻击拦截率稳定在 92%，而目录级漏洞率从 10 个工具时的 22% 上升至 200 个工具时的 99%，且策略组合并未带来任何保护作用；一项涉及 15 个模型的清单编写试点实验表明，真实错误按作者聚集，因此一个包含 200 个工具的目录的行为大约相当于 5 个独立决策……
tldr: 该论文指出“单攻击拦截率”是错误的评估单位——工具目录的漏洞率随独立编写的策略数量按 1-(1-p)^M 增长（从 10 个工具的 22% 升至 200 个工具的 99%），而单攻击拦截率始终保持在约 92%，因此安全性应按目录级“最弱环节”而非单次攻击拦截来衡量。
en_tdlr: The paper shows that per-attack blocking is the wrong evaluation unit for tool-manifest security: catalog vulnerability grows as 1-(1-p)^M with independently authored policies—rising from 22% at 10 tools to 99% at 200—while per-attack blocking stays flat at 92%.
